title: Goods and services businesses
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-goods-services, covers only goods versus services, while the new point also requires grouping businesses into primary, secondary and tertiary industries, which is a different idea the card does not teach.

draft.title: Goods and services businesses
card: things you can touch, such as shoes, bread or a phone. A business that makes or sells them is a goods business.
work done for you, such as a haircut, a bus ride or a music lesson. You cannot hold a service in your hands.
Businesses can also be grouped by industry. Primary industries take natural resources from the land or sea, such as farming, fishing and mining.
Secondary industries turn materials into products, such as a factory making furniture. Tertiary industries provide services, such as banking, teaching and retail.
draft.remember: Goods are things you can touch and services are work done for you. Primary takes resources, secondary makes products, tertiary serves.

a.q: Which business mainly sells a service?
opts: A dog grooming salon in Geelong
a.why: Grooming is work done for a customer, so it is a service. A bakery, a shoe shop and a bike factory all provide things you can touch, which are goods.
a.clue: Which one sells work done for you, not an object?

b.q: Priya's company in Mildura turns tomatoes from local farms into jars of pasta sauce. Which industry is her business in?
opts: Secondary, because it turns materials into a product
Primary, because tomatoes come from farms
Tertiary, because it sells to supermarkets
Tertiary, because jars of sauce are goods
b.why: Priya's business takes materials and makes them into a new product, which is secondary industry. The tomatoes are grown by farmers in the primary industry, but Priya does not grow them.
b.clue: Look at what Priya's business does with the tomatoes.

a.best: A dog grooming salon in Geelong

b.best: Secondary, because it turns materials into a product
